title: Learned cell-death signature associates with lung cancer survival
summary: LASSO and random-forest screening identified a five-gene programmed-cell-death index in 500 lung-adenocarcinoma cases. Higher scores were associated with poorer overall survival, with similar associations in three public external cohorts. Separate tissue staining examined selected model genes. Drug sensitivity and immunotherapy response were computational estimates, rather than demonstrated treatment effects or clinical benefit.
organization: Shandong University; Shandong First Medical University

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Retrospective survival associations of a learned five-gene signature in TCGA and three additional GEO cohorts; selected protein-expression checks in tissue.
evidence.unknown: Prospective clinical utility, treatment-response prediction and causal roles of the signature remain unestablished; cohort-specific thresholds and retrospective selection limit interpretation.
evidence.ai_role: Penalized regression and random-forest selection prioritize genes for an outcome-linked expression signature, enabling survival-association analyses.
